thesis: This episode argues that investors should focus on the underlying business and predictable cash flows of well-run companies rather than macro factors or market distortions. It uses examples like McDonald's and Walmart to illustrate that micro factors often dominate macro factors, while also noting that stock prices can swing wildly due to auction-driven market distortions even when the business hasn't changed. The speaker also shares personal investment experiences, including a $65 million loss on Delta Financial, to emphasize the importance of rigorous business analysis.
